terms.definition: `ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/`: resources added, removed, changed (with an element-level differential) and version-changed; edges added and removed; the plan's decision. Every page opens with the provisional mark and is wrapped in raw so narrative Liquid is not executed.

terms.prefLabel: Note the missed coupling on the bean [todo-manager]
terms.definition: Append to bean `a9tx` (W8): the resource key, the differential path, and why it is unexplained. Check before creating: beans create is not idempotent. A note, not a new bean, unless the owner asks for one.

Start at the delta index; open each changed resource's page. Check `builtAt` before judging: a resource carried from the base was not rebuilt, so a difference there is the change itself or a missed coupling, never noise. The differential is structural: a reordered repeating element shows at every index.

terms.definition: `ig-ast.ts validity <base> --ig <root>`: folio-assistant-core's compiledValidity on the manifest's inputs, with the input digest recomputed by the same algorithm as the Java writer. Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (names which input), 2 cannot-tell. Run against the BASE revision's checkout.

terms.prefLabel: Restricted checkout of the backward cone
terms.definition: git sparse-checkout of the cone's files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, on smart-immunizations.

terms.prefLabel: Compute the cone of the change (fsh-cone --changed)
terms.definition: content/pipeline/fsh-cone.ts over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out.

terms.prefLabel: Post the cone report on the PR
terms.definition: Review path: the reviewer sees what this change rebuilds — how many artefacts, and whether a hub (a shared RuleSet, CQL library or value set) is touched — before the build finishes. On main it is a log line.

terms.prefLabel: Load or reuse the warm context (fhir_context_load)
terms.definition: The validator's server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it.

Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site.
A preview never seeds the shared cache.
Exit 1 or 3 from restore: the whole IG is built as today. Its outputs become the records the next seed writes.
The whole-IG aggregates only — artifacts, TOC, canonicals, expansions, package, QA aggregate. Never re-derives an artefact: a missing record is a miss (exit 1), not a silent rebuild.

terms.prefLabel: Log the environment error on the bean [todo-manager]
terms.definition: Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change's bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent.
Validation failed: record the findings on the change's bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent.
Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one.

terms.prefLabel: QC gates on the aggregate QA [quality-control]
terms.definition: qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone's rows first.
QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one.

terms.prefLabel: Re-render the cone's records (fhir_narrative · skip lists)
terms.definition: Narrative and fragments for the cone only: the publisher's -no-validate / -no-narrative complements today, Rapido's differential build once its tracker is persisted.
ig-cache restore: per-artefact records, the terminology cache, the package cache and temp/, keyed by the toolchain slug. Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but toolchain moved.

terms.prefLabel: Seed the cache from the green build (ig-cache seed · verify · promote)
terms.definition: Only a green build of main or a release seeds. Seed writes to the -test branch, verifies a restore from a clean clone, then promotes.
Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists.

Compile the restricted checkout with SUSHI — the cone's FSH, not the whole IG. A build optimisation, not a validation shortcut: SUSHI compiling is not conformance, so a green compile goes on to validation rather than standing in for it.

Validate the cone's resources against the warm validator and report the cone that was checked. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with no findings. A green cone is not a green IG: a profile the change did not touch can still be broken by it.

Write the FSH profiles, value sets and definitions the L2 mapping calls for. This is the stage where profiles, slicing and invariants belong — a decision that can only be expressed in FHIR comes here, not back into L2.

Run the IG Publisher: it renders output/, writes each resource's JSON, the package, canonicals and qa.json, and does the two things no cache can — validates every resource against its profiles and resolves the dependency closure with terminology expansion.

Each data element becomes a profile, each value set a ValueSet, each decision a PlanDefinition / Library. The DAK's L2 content is l3-fhir-authoring's sourceModel; this step binds l2-dak-authoring beside it, which is where the WHO L2 → L3 ordering lives now that the generic skill names no DAK (smart-* separation stage D, #1767).
Release authorisation and review follow draft-to-publication.bpmn.
QC findings do not stay in a report nobody re-reads — each becomes a bean the modeller and the agents both see.

The QC reviewer rules on the aggregate QA against the publication gates. Emitting the QA report is mechanical; ruling on it is a decision, which is why it sits in the reviewer's lane rather than the build's.
Compile the FSH to FHIR JSON with SUSHI. Compiling is not conformance: a green SUSHI result goes on to validation and never stands in for it.

Validate the compiled resources against their profiles and the packages they constrain. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with an empty findings list. Failures return to authoring.
